_comment: Quishing: a credential lure whose entire payload is a QR code. The
teaching case for the attachment channel, and the reason it exists —
every URL-based defense in the pipeline has NOTHING to bite on. The
message body carries no links at all, so there is no href for the
gateway to rewrite, nothing for URL reputation to score, and nothing
for a user to hover over. The destination is printed as pixels, and
the click happens on a phone camera, off the managed endpoint, where
neither the proxy nor the EDR is watching.
Authentication is not the discriminator here and is deliberately not
made to fail: the attacker owns ms-authenticator-support.com and
configured it correctly, so SPF, DKIM and DMARC all pass and align.
What gives it away is what authentication never covers — a display
name claiming a brand the sending domain is not authorized to send
as, and a QR destination that puts the real brand's hostname in the
SUBDOMAIN of a site the attacker controls, with the recipient's own
address carried along so the fake portal arrives pre-filled.
Its benign twin is benign_qr_mfa_enrollment.json: the same event
shape, the same QR-code-in-an-image delivery, the same MFA-enrollment
pretext, opposite verdict. The discriminator is where the QR points.
